verdict: Prefer one explicit bounded prefill_pipeline command over per-chunk preissue. It reuses unchanged phased_forward and native collective scheduling; one ACK after all nonfinal chunks, then ordinary final-token forward. Under rendezvous it overlaps rank1 next target chunk with rank0 current target and shifted MTP head, with at most two chunk epochs resident/in progress. Actual installed API does NOT document receiver-consumed rendezvous: strict <=2 outstanding-chunk admission requires stronger transport proof or one receive-credit per chunk at the existing receive-before-GPU seam.

old_dependency_graph: rank0 begin CMD_i(length then JSON) <-> rank1 receive CMD_i
rank1 embed_i -> owned native layers_i + evaluated owned caches_i -> evaluated CPU SEND(hidden_i)
rank0 evaluated RECV(hidden_i) -> owned native layers_i + evaluated owned caches_i -> norm_i (024 hidden-only;023 full norm+vocab)
rank1 SEND(hidden_i) return -> dispatch return -> Worker ACK_i -> evaluated CPU SEND(ACK_i); under rendezvous this ACK waits while rank0 executes local target
rank0 target_i return -> RECV/validate ACK_i -> rank_action_i -> shifted head_i and evaluated head KV -> begin CMD_i+1
Consequently rank1 next chunk cannot begin before rank0 entire current target/head returns. Removing discarded vocabulary projection alone does not remove this barrier.
recommended_compound_protocol: Admit explicit opt-in and same-process pipeline numerical capability on BOTH ranks. Existing hidden-only capability alone is insufficient. Freeze same-source disabled/enabled serial-hidden-only controls.

Reset exactly as before and receive its ACK. Rank0 sends one prefill_pipeline Command(request,sequence,tokens=full bounded prompt), command length and JSON are received by rank1 before either starts hidden traffic.

Validate prompt token IDs against actual vocabulary, 1<=length<=2048 (or bypass compound for length1), derive immutable chunk bounds range(0,len(prompt)-1,256); final prompt ID is metadata only here. Do not let whole-prompt transport imply whole-prompt forward arithmetic.

Rank1 dispatch loops those chunks in order through unchanged native phased_forward(logits=False). Each chunk evaluates all owned caches and CPU-send result. No Channel frames and no ACK are interleaved inside this raw-hidden loop in the simple version.

Rank0 dispatch loops exactly the same bounds through unchanged phased_forward(logits=False,return_hidden=True,all_logits=True); immediately head.forward(normalized_hidden,prompt[start+1:end+1],same_mtp_cache,position=start,logits=False). Fully evaluate head before next rank0 chunk; drop prior temporary hidden refs. Rank1 next chunk is independent of rank0 current head.

Under synchronous rendezvous: rank0 RECV hidden_i releases rank1 SEND_i; rank1 computes i+1 while rank0 does local target_i and head_i; rank1 next SEND waits for rank0 next RECV. Thus no nonblocking send, queue or second CPU stream is required.

Only after rank1 entire prefix loop returns does Worker emit ONE ACK for the compound command. Rank0 drains and validates this ACK only AFTER its entire prefix/head loop completes. For the last prefix send, rank1 may block sending this ACK while rank0 computes last local target/head; that is intentional and safe.

After compound ACK, require target prefix offsets len(prompt)-1 on each KV layer and head KV offset len(prompt)-1. Then send ordinary forward([prompt[-1]]) exactly once, with original ACK and final projection/argmax/TTFT boundary. No head-prefill call on final prompt hidden; first draft pairs that hidden with first generated token as before.

On ordinary prefill/decode/snapshot/rollback/finish keep existing op names, sequence, numerical modes, cache order and validation; one compound consumes one command sequence, not one per internal chunk. Audit expands only this known compound into the exact trusted prefix intervals.

bounds_and_state.rendezvous_bound: Rank0 current chunk and rank1 next chunk; rank1 cannot complete send of next until rank0 receives it. Per-rank target caches intentionally differ by up to one chunk; compare corresponding logical boundaries, not contemporaneous offsets.
bounds_and_state.actual_transport_caveat: Installed mlx0.32.3 distributed.pyi:158-174 only says send is performed when output is evaluated. The installed ring.h contains declarations only; distributed_impl.h:27/45 is an abstract send API. These plain files do not certify receiver-consumed semantics. An evaluated blocking send could still complete after copying into bounded TCP/kernel buffers. Then rank1 may run ahead more than one chunk despite no Python queue; the compound is still finite (8 prefix chunks), but strict in-flight<=2 is not established.
bounds_and_state.strict_bound_fallback: If no exact deployed ring backend proof exists, add one tiny request/sequence/chunk-tagged receive-credit: rank0 sends credit_i immediately AFTER evaluated hidden receive_i and BEFORE constructing its local GPU graph; rank1 waits for credit_i AFTER evaluated send_i and BEFORE next embedding. This is a credit, not a completion ACK. Keep one final compound ACK. It guarantees <=2 logical chunk epochs with eager OR rendezvous transport. Needs one explicit receive-boundary hook, no new thread/stream and no arithmetic change. Alternatively return to per-command preissue at the same receive-boundary, with more ACK/descriptor state.

preissue_alternative.correct_order: receive/evaluate current hidden -> receive and validate CURRENT ACK_i (rank1 has returned from current send/dispatch) -> send NEXT command -> compute rank0 current target/native norm -> shifted head current -> receive next hidden. Do not receive next ACK before its hidden. Store current ACK so _command does not finish it twice.
preissue_alternative.safe_lower_gain: A smaller begin-next-after-_command-current but before head-current change retains current ACK order and avoids forward hook, but overlaps ONLY next rank1 target with current MTP head, not with rank0 target layers. Archived current head-adjacent gap is small compared with local target work; 30% TTFT is not a supported hypothesis for that tiny-only overlap.
preissue_alternative.comparison: Compound is simpler and mirrors physically exercised native collective prefill, keeps ordinary phased_forward intact, eliminates per-chunk controls and ACK drain state. Prefer compound if finite prompt bound suffices or rendezvous is established; use receive-credit compound for unconditional strict<=2. Do not deploy a bare compound while claiming a rendezvous bound that has not been established.

deadlocks_and_failures: Preissue before current hidden receive: rank0 blocks sending next command while rank1 blocks sending current hidden.
Preissue after hidden but before current ACK drain: rank0 command SEND and rank1 ACK SEND both rendezvous waiting.

Expect per-chunk ACK inside simple compound: rank0 consumes raw hidden as frame-length or waits for ACK while rank1 waits for next hidden receive. Shared CPU-stream ordering makes this fatal, not merely slow.
Send final ordinary forward before draining compound ACK: symmetric SEND/SEND deadlock.

Insert credit only after local target or head without matching sender wait/ordering: can reserialize or cause send/send deadlock; the full-overlap credit must be at evaluated receive before local graph.
Rank1/0 disagree on prompt length, chunk cap, bounds, op capability or final singleton: mismatched raw recv shape/count, cache divergence or deadlock. Admit before first hidden operation.

Any rank exception while peer is in raw hidden send/recv: do not try a normal JSON error ACK on the raw tensor channel or enqueue reset/finish. Fail closed and let existing owned bounded supervisor deadline/cleanup act; never claim recoverable request protocol without explicit abort design.
Do not wait for a peer ACK on a GPU stream, change default streams, introduce worker threads around process-global numerical_mode hooks, or retain full prompt activation queues.

evidence.existing_reuse: Native phased_generate is working evidence of the same direct collective loop and no per-chunk command barrier on this source/runtime; archived rank1 own-clock gaps below confirm immediate next-stage starts. It is NOT evidence that MTP head overlap preserves all states, that ring send consumption is rendezvous, or that candidate meets requested thresholds.
evidence.clock_rule: Use only within-rank monotonic durations and causal command/hidden/ACK IDs. Never subtract rank0 timestamps from rank1 timestamps; receive wall time includes upstream compute, Python and waiting, not cable transfer time.
evidence.concurrent_progress_observables: Bind each internal chunk to request+compound sequence+chunk index+start/end; record synchronized embedding/block/cache completion and rank0 norm/head completion. Under rendezvous/receive-credit, rank1 send_i -> embedding_i+1 gaps should collapse while rank0 current target/head still completes normally; next SEND wait is expected bounded backpressure. For offset-independent overlap witness, rank0 measures full compound epoch from BEFORE sending command to AFTER draining final ACK. Both ranks local synchronized target-block/head intervals are causally contained in that epoch. If their nonoverlapping-within-rank duration sum exceeds epoch duration beyond measured CPU/reporting/clock-rate uncertainty, stage execution envelopes overlap without clock-offset subtraction. This establishes concurrent stage progress, not exact GPU kernel occupancy.
evidence.gpu_caveat: Existing before/done wall events bracket mx.eval and cache completion, so they show real synchronized work, but include graph construction, synchronization and host overhead. CPU-command timestamps or a small send-gap alone cannot prove simultaneous Metal kernels. Strict GPU-kernel concurrency requires per-device GPU timelines plus bounded common-epoch/clock calibration or equivalent device evidence; do not claim that from present logs.
evidence.receipt_budget: Keep compact per-chunk integer/phase/dtype/shape/offset summaries, constant-size rolling digest and max-inflight counters, never arrays or repeated whole prompt/metric trees per chunk. For2048 prompt <=8 prefix chunks. Enforce frame65536, actor log64MiB and retrieval128MiB plus controller limits; current candidate rank1.stderr about59MB leaves little64MiB headroom. Budget pilot before full suite and reject overflow, never truncate.

performance_hypothesis.claim: Plausible for genuine target-stage overlap, not demonstrated. Scope cannot promise30% on every long case or15% complete request.
performance_hypothesis.why: Archived enabled-hidden-only MTP rank1 first two blocks per256chunk total roughly2.2s while rank0 native block is roughly1.6-1.7s plus a small head update. Six prefix chunks offer a sizeable serial bubble; same-trial native collective runs show near-zero send-done -> next-embedding gaps instead of ~1.7s warm MTP gaps.
performance_hypothesis.ideal_formula: For constant stage costs A(rank1) and B(rank0 target+head), K prefix chunks: serial K*(A+B); perfect two-stage pipeline A+B+(K-1)*max(A,B), plus unchanged final singleton/control overhead. No isolated phase addition is used as a measured speedup.
performance_hypothesis.end_to_end_condition: If only prefill changes, absolute saved time Delta must satisfy Delta>=0.30*baseline_TTFT and Delta>=0.15*baseline_wall for EACH case. Decode/output work and final singleton remain. Contention, shape/thermal warming, imbalance and actual transport can erase ideal gain; native no-head TTFT is not the candidate forecast.
